_about: Rulebook of common customs-hold causes and document-readiness checks. Requirements are paraphrased from the cited official pages (rules/sources.json); they are a study aid for a portfolio project, not legal or customs advice. status: 'verified' = the requirement as written was found in the cited source; 'partially verified' = the core requirement was found but a detail used here (a tolerance, a base, a mapping) was not; 'not verified' = no cited source states it (derived rule or common practice). docs/rule_check.md is the second, independent check of every rule.

rules.title: Customs import permit before the goods are imported
rules.requirement: The importer must obtain the relevant customs permit before the goods are imported into Singapore; the permit is submitted through TradeNet. The overview's 'common errors' section explains how a wrong permit is corrected depending on whether it has already been used for clearance.
rules.readiness_check: Permit application timestamp is earlier than the arrival date of the shipment.
rules.corrective_action: Apply for the permit before re-presenting the cargo; for later shipments the handling note asks for the permit before arrival. If goods were imported without a permit, the error can only be corrected through a voluntary disclosure (SG-IMP-27).
rules.status_note: The timing comes from the overview and the TradeNet route from the permit page; neither page alone states both. The second-pass check found that the first version wrongly said an unused or used permit is itself listed as an error; corrected.

rules.title: UEN from ACRA and an activated Customs account
rules.requirement: An importer first registers with ACRA (or the relevant UEN issuance agency) to obtain a UEN and then activates a Customs account with Singapore Customs; the activation is needed before any import permit application can be submitted. A declaring agent may apply for permits on the importer's behalf.
rules.readiness_check: Customer profile has a UEN and the Customs account is recorded as activated before the first permit is drafted.
rules.corrective_action: Ask the customer to activate the Customs account (or confirm activation) before the first shipment; hold the enrolment at 'Documents received' until confirmed.

sources.where: UEN and Customs account section; Declaring Agent section

rules.title: UEN format
rules.requirement: Entity UEN formats: businesses registered with ACRA NNNNNNNNC (9 characters); local companies YYYYNNNNNC (10 characters), with foreign companies listed under the same entry as F000NNNNNC or FDDDNNNNNC (D = a space); other entities TYYPQNNNNC or SYYPQNNNNC (10 characters). N is a digit, C a check letter, YYYY or TYY/SYY a year (T = 20, S = 19) and PQ an entity-type code.
rules.readiness_check: UEN on the enrolment form matches one of the three patterns.
rules.corrective_action: Request the UEN as shown on the ACRA business profile; do not draft permits until it is on file.

sources.where: Section II - TIN structure, entity ID types

rules.status_note: Formats verified against the OECD TIN sheet that Singapore supplied; the agency page it links to (uen.gov.sg) returned HTTP 403, and the check-letter algorithm is not published there, so only the pattern is checked, not the check letter or whether the UEN exists. The second-pass check found that the first version omitted the foreign-company formats; they were added.
assumptions: Only the character pattern is validated; the check letter and the registration year are not.

rules.title: Correct importer name and UEN on the permit
rules.requirement: Wrong importer name and UEN, and wrong importer, are listed as common permit errors. A UEN must not be used to import goods that do not belong to that entity, except when consolidating for customers without a UEN, in which case the consolidator remains responsible.
rules.readiness_check: Importer UEN and name on the draft permit equal the customer profile.
rules.corrective_action: Amend the importer fields while the permit is valid, or cancel and re-apply if the field is not amendable (SG-IMP-26); correct the customer master data.
rules.status_note: The two errors appear in the overview's sub-lists for Major Exporter Scheme traders and for In-Payment permits.

rules.title: HS code valid in STCCED 2022 (8-digit AHTN, based on HS 2022)
rules.requirement: The permit HS code must be a valid code of the Singapore Trade Classification, Customs and Excise Duties (STCCED) publication, and Singapore's current schedule is STCCED 2022. Separately, the same page describes the ASEAN Harmonised Tariff Nomenclature (AHTN) as an 8-digit nomenclature used by all ASEAN member states, based on the WCO 6-digit HS, whose 2022 amendment incorporated the HS 2022 changes.
rules.readiness_check: HS code is 8 digits and its first 6 digits are an HS 2022 subheading.
rules.corrective_action: Correct the code in the product master and the permit (amend while valid). For doubtful cases use the HS/CA Product Code Checker or apply for a classification ruling (SG-IMP-14).
rules.status_note: The requirement is verified. The page does not itself say that STCCED 2022 is built on AHTN 2022 (that link is this project's reading). The check uses only the public HS 2022 6-digit list: the national 7th-8th digits are not validated because the STCCED code list is not used here.
assumptions: Validity is tested at the 6-digit level only.

rules.title: HS quantity and unit as prescribed in STCCED
rules.requirement: Each permit item carries a quantity and unit-of-quantity code as prescribed in STCCED; competent authorities may require their own product-code quantity and unit.
rules.readiness_check: Manual: unit on invoice and packing list can be converted to the STCCED unit of the HS code.
rules.corrective_action: Ask for a packing list that states the quantity in the prescribed unit.

sources.where: Inward fields, 37 HS quantity and unit; 8 CA/SC product code quantity and unit

rules.status_note: Not automated: the STCCED unit table is not part of this repository.

rules.title: Customs value on a CIF basis, including incidental charges
rules.requirement: Transaction value is the primary valuation method and is based on the CIF value. All charges incidental to the sale and delivery of the goods to Singapore are included, e.g. selling commissions, assists, packing, royalties and licence fees, freight and insurance; an EXW price additionally needs inland transport, port handling and export clearance costs. Wrong value is a common error and an incorrect value declaration an offence.
rules.readiness_check: CIF value computed from the invoice and the charges required by its Incoterm equals the value on the draft permit within tolerance.
rules.corrective_action: Recompute the CIF value and amend the permit while it is valid; if the permit has been used for clearance, submit a voluntary disclosure (SG-IMP-26, SG-IMP-27).

sources.where: transaction value; charges to include; EXW example
'Do' list (include freight and insurance); 'Common errors' and 'Offences' lists

rules.status_note: Requirement verified. The comparison tolerance (0.5% of CIF, minimum SGD 1) is an assumption of this project.
assumptions: Value tolerance 0.5% of the computed CIF value (minimum SGD 1).

rules.title: Flat freight-and-insurance rates for FOB imports with unknown charges
rules.requirement: When the transaction value is quoted FOB and the actual freight and insurance are not known or not available to the importer, flat rates of the FOB value may be used, by place of export: Africa, Canada and USA 24.5%; Europe 19%; Japan, Australia and New Zealand 19%; China, Chinese Taipei, Korea, Sri Lanka, India and Pakistan 15.5%; Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, Hong Kong, Philippines and Indonesia 9.5%; Peninsular Malaysia 5%.
rules.readiness_check: FOB invoice without actual charges: CIF = FOB x (1 + flat rate of the export country); other export countries need actual charges.
rules.corrective_action: Add the flat-rate amount, or obtain the freight and insurance invoices.
rules.status_note: Rates and conditions verified; the page does not say whether the rates differ by transport mode. The country-to-region mapping in rules/sg_flat_freight_insurance.csv is this project's reading of the table (e.g. Germany as Europe).
assumptions: The flat rate is applied regardless of mode (the page names no mode).
Malaysian exports are assumed to leave from Peninsular Malaysia.

rules.title: Flat 1% insurance for CFR imports with unknown insurance
rules.requirement: When the transaction value is quoted CFR and the actual insurance cost is unknown or unavailable, a flat insurance rate of 1% may be used to compute the customs value; if no insurance was bought, the insurance cost may be declared as zero.
rules.readiness_check: CFR invoice without an insurance amount: insurance = 1% of the CFR value unless the customer confirms no insurance was bought.
rules.corrective_action: Add the 1% insurance or a statement that no insurance was purchased.
rules.status_note: Rate and conditions verified; the page does not state the base of the 1%. This project applies it to the CFR value.
assumptions: Base of the 1% = CFR invoice value.

rules.title: Foreign-currency amounts converted at MAS weekly average rates
rules.requirement: Costs in foreign currency are converted to Singapore dollars at the prevailing weekly average MAS exchange rates; the permit-field guide says the rates of the preceding week are used for declarations made in the current week.
rules.readiness_check: Invoice currency is stated; the conversion uses the rate of the week before the declaration.
rules.corrective_action: Request an invoice that states its currency.
rules.status_note: The synthetic data use fixed ILLUSTRATIVE exchange rates (config/synth_assumptions.json), not MAS rates.

rules.title: GST on all imports: rate x (customs value + duties)
rules.requirement: All goods imported into Singapore are subject to GST at the prevailing rate. For dutiable goods GST = rate x (customs value or last selling price + duties payable); for non-dutiable goods GST = rate x customs value (or last selling price).
rules.readiness_check: Estimated GST on the draft permit = 9% x (CIF value in SGD + duty).
rules.corrective_action: Recompute GST after any value correction.
rules.status_note: Last selling price cases are not modelled.

rules.title: GST rate 9%
rules.requirement: The current GST rate in Singapore is 9%; IRAS's table of past rates shows 8% for 1 January to 31 December 2023.
rules.readiness_check: GST estimates use 9%.

sources.where: current rate statement; rate history table

rules.title: Dutiable goods: liquor, tobacco, motor vehicles, petroleum products
rules.requirement: Customs and excise duties apply to four categories: intoxicating liquors, tobacco products, motor vehicles, and petroleum products and biodiesel blends. Other goods are non-dutiable but GST may still apply.
rules.readiness_check: Lines in HS chapters/headings mapped to these categories are flagged 'dutiable: duty rate and quantity fields needed'.
rules.corrective_action: Declare duty rate and dutiable quantity; consider preference only with proof of origin (SG-IMP-22).
rules.status_note: Categories verified. The HS mapping (2203-2208, 24, 2710, 8703) in rules/sg_ca_screening.csv is a screening heuristic of this project.
assumptions: Dutiable screening by HS heading, not by the exact STCCED duty column.

rules.title: Controlled goods need competent-authority approval before import
rules.requirement: Controlled goods need authorisation from the relevant Competent Authority (advance notification, licence or certificate approval) before they may be imported. The HS/CA Product Code Checker shows whether an HS code is controlled and by which CA; uncertain classifications can be put to Singapore Customs for an official ruling.
rules.readiness_check: Lines whose HS prefix appears in the CA screening table need a CA licence or approval reference on file.
rules.corrective_action: Obtain the CA licence/approval, record its number in the handling note, then re-submit; confirm the CA product code with the HS/CA Product Code Checker.

sources.where: HS/CA Product Code Checker; 'Still unsure' section

rules.status_note: Requirement verified. Screening by HS chapter/heading is this project's heuristic; the authoritative test is the HS/CA product code, which is not used here.

rules.title: Competent authorities and what they control
rules.requirement: Singapore Customs lists 14 competent authorities for controlled items: BCA (sand and granite), CNB (controlled substances), Enterprise Singapore (rubber exports), GRA (fruit and jackpot machines), HSA (health products), IMDA (publications, telecommunication equipment), LTA (PABs and motorised PMDs), MOH (biological agents and toxins), NEA (wastes, hazardous substances and chemicals, ODS, HFCs, radioactive materials, irradiating apparatus), NParks (CITES specimens, plants, live animals, animal products, ornamental fish), SCDF (petroleum and flammable materials), Singapore Customs (regulated goods and sanctioned trade), SFA (fruit, vegetables, livestock, animal products, meat, salted/preserved eggs and processed egg products, processed food, rice, fish) and SPF (GEW-regulated items; amusement game machines).
rules.readiness_check: The CA named by the screening table is written into the handling note with the licence type to ask for.
rules.status_note: The list is verified as written above. The expansions used elsewhere in this project, PAB = power-assisted bicycle and GEW = guns, explosives and weapons, are this project's reading; the page uses only the abbreviations. The first version also named eggs in general under SFA; corrected.

rules.title: HSA: health products that need licensing or approval; cosmetics do not
rules.requirement: HSA licensing and/or approval before import applies to therapeutic products, medical devices, cell, tissue and gene therapy products, Chinese proprietary medicines, clinical-research products, controlled drugs and psychotropic substances, oral dental gums, poisons and active ingredients. Cosmetic products, health supplements, quasi-medicines and several traditional medicines are currently not subject to HSA licensing before importation. Declarations use an HSA product code and the licence details in the CA/SC code fields.
rules.readiness_check: Chapter 30 and medical-device headings require an HSA licence reference; chapter 33 (cosmetics) is not flagged.
rules.corrective_action: Ask for the HSA licence/approval and product code before the first shipment.

sources.where: Table 1; list of products not currently controlled; product code table

rules.title: SFA: food imports need a licence or registration and a permit before arrival
rules.requirement: SFA controls imports of fruit and vegetables (licence), livestock and animal products (permit in advance), meat (licence for meat and fish products, a permit for every consignment of meat product, veterinary health certificate), salted/preserved eggs and processed egg products (from SFA-approved establishments, with a health certificate), processed food and food appliances (registration), rice (licence) and fish (licence, permit per consignment, health certificates for some items). The customs permit must be obtained before the goods arrive.
rules.readiness_check: Food chapters require an SFA licence/registration reference; meat and seafood lines also need a health certificate on file.
rules.corrective_action: Ask for the SFA licence or registration number and the exporting country's health certificate.
rules.status_note: The second-pass check found that the first version applied the meat licence, permit and veterinary certificate to egg products as well; corrected. The health-certificate check is applied to chapters 02 and 03 only.
assumptions: Health certificate requirement screened at chapters 02 and 03.

rules.title: IMDA: telecommunication equipment is declared to IMDA
rules.requirement: All imported telecommunication equipment must be declared to IMDA through TradeNet before arrival; dealers need an IMDA telecommunication dealer's licence and enter the licence number, product code and equipment registration number; some equipment needs prior IMDA approval. Publications are also controlled.
rules.readiness_check: Headings 8517 and 8525-8529 require an IMDA dealer's licence reference (or an own-use declaration).
rules.corrective_action: Ask for the dealer's licence number and equipment registration numbers.

sources.where: Telecommunication Equipment sections A and B; Publications

rules.status_note: The heading list is this project's screening choice.

rules.title: NEA: hazardous substances, ODS/HFCs, radioactive materials, wastes
rules.requirement: NEA requires a hazardous substances licence for items containing EPMA-listed ingredients, an import licence for controlled ozone-depleting substances and HFCs, radiation licences for radioactive materials and irradiating apparatus, and a Basel permit for controlled hazardous waste; the customs permit is obtained before arrival.
rules.readiness_check: Chemical chapters (28, 29, 38) and heading 9022 require a licence reference or a statement that the substance is not controlled.
rules.corrective_action: Ask for the NEA licence number, or the safety data sheet showing the substance is not controlled.
rules.status_note: Chapter-level screening over-flags: most chemicals in chapters 28, 29 and 38 are not NEA-controlled.

rules.title: Prohibited imports
rules.requirement: Goods that cannot be imported include chewing gum (other than HSA-approved oral dental and medicinal gum), rhinoceros horn and endangered wildlife products, certain telecommunication equipment such as jammers and scanning receivers, imitation tobacco products including e-cigarettes and vaporisers, other listed tobacco and nicotine products, and controlled drugs listed in the 4th Schedule of the Misuse of Drugs Regulations.
rules.readiness_check: Lines in heading 1704.10 (chewing gum) or subheading 8543.40 (e-cigarettes) are flagged 'prohibited: do not accept for import'.
rules.corrective_action: Do not lodge; inform the customer that the goods cannot be imported.
rules.status_note: The list is verified; the two HS codes used for screening are this project's mapping.

rules.title: Country of origin is where goods were wholly obtained or substantially transformed
rules.requirement: The origin field is the country or region in which the goods were wholly obtained or substantially transformed, meeting the rules of origin of that place. Declaring the country of the port of loading as the origin when the goods originate elsewhere is on the 'do not' list.
rules.readiness_check: Every invoice line states a country of origin; if the origin equals the port-of-loading country while the certificate of origin or supplier declaration names another country, flag a mismatch.
rules.corrective_action: Ask the supplier to confirm origin; amend the permit.

rules.title: FTA preference on dutiable imports needs proof of origin
rules.requirement: Lower or zero duty under an FTA applies to certain dutiable goods originating in a partner country. Proof of origin is a preferential certificate of origin, a self-certification, or an electronic reference (e.g. e-ATIGA Form D). With proof at import the permit uses preference indicator 'PRF'; the CO or self-certification, invoice and bill of lading go to Singapore Customs within 1 week of clearance. Without proof, full duty is paid and a refund may be requested within 1 year.
rules.readiness_check: If preference is claimed, a CO or self-certification is on file.
rules.corrective_action: Obtain the CO; if it is not available at import, pay the full duty, note the intention in Remarks and claim the refund within 1 year.

sources.where: proof of origin; declaring in TradeNet; time limits

rules.title: Invoice data the permit needs
rules.requirement: The permit carries the commercial invoice number and date, the goods description as on the invoice, the total invoice amount with currency and exchange rate (excluding freight, insurance and other taxable charges when these are shown separately), item values on CIF terms for imports, and, for goods with ad valorem duty, the unit price with its currency and term type.
rules.readiness_check: Invoice has number, date, seller, buyer, currency, Incoterm, and for every line a description, quantity, unit, unit price, line value and origin.
rules.corrective_action: Request a corrected commercial invoice from the supplier; add the missing fields to the customer's invoice checklist in the handling note.
rules.status_note: Invoice number and date, description, currency, total and item values are verified field requirements. Seller and buyer name on the invoice are common practice, not stated in the cited guide.
assumptions: Seller and buyer names are required by this project's checklist.

rules.title: Incoterm stated on the invoice
rules.requirement: Derived rule: what must be added to the invoice price to reach the CIF value depends on the delivery term (EXW needs inland and export costs; FOB needs freight and insurance; CFR needs insurance), and the flat rates apply only to FOB or CFR quotes. An invoice that does not state its Incoterm therefore cannot be valued without asking.
rules.readiness_check: Invoice states an Incoterms 2020 rule (and named place).
rules.corrective_action: Ask the supplier to state the Incoterm on the invoice.
rules.status_note: No cited page states 'the invoice must show an Incoterm' as a requirement; the rule is inferred from the valuation pages. The permit's term-type field (Module 5 field 90) applies only to dutiable goods with ad valorem duty, so it does not support a general requirement either; the second-pass check agreed.

rules.title: Supporting documents to the declaring agent; keep for 5 years
rules.requirement: Provide full supporting documents (invoices, shipping documents, certificates of origin) to the declaring agent; failing to produce trade documents on request is an offence; supporting documents are kept for 5 years.
rules.readiness_check: Commercial invoice, packing list and bill of lading or air waybill are on file before the permit is drafted.
rules.corrective_action: Request the missing document; record the document checklist in the handling note.
rules.status_note: The page names invoices, shipping documents and certificates of origin; the packing list is common practice and is not named there.
assumptions: Packing list required by this project's checklist.

rules.title: Amend while valid; cancel and re-apply for non-amendable fields
rules.requirement: An approved permit can be amended in TradeNet while it is valid, any number of times, except non-amendable fields. Incorrect details in non-amendable fields are corrected by cancelling the valid permit and applying for a new one. A permit used for cargo clearance or expired cannot be amended; a permit used for cargo clearance, expired for more than 1 calendar day, or requested for audit by the Manifest Compliance Unit cannot be cancelled, and for such cases the page points to a voluntary disclosure.
rules.readiness_check: Corrective action chosen by permit state: valid -> amend (or cancel and re-apply for a non-amendable field); expired by at most 1 calendar day -> cancel and re-apply; used for clearance or expired longer -> voluntary disclosure; under a Customs check -> respond to the check, because a voluntary disclosure must come before any Customs check (SG-IMP-27).
rules.corrective_action: See readiness_check.
rules.status_note: The second-pass check found that the first version treated every expired permit as needing a voluntary disclosure; the 1-calendar-day cancellation window and the audit case were added.

rules.title: Voluntary disclosure of declaration errors
rules.requirement: Traders are encouraged to disclose errors or omissions in their declarations through the Voluntary Disclosure Programme; the disclosure must be complete and made before Singapore Customs initiates checks, audits or investigations, and some situations are excluded.
rules.readiness_check: For holds found after clearance, the action log records a voluntary disclosure step.
rules.corrective_action: Prepare a complete disclosure with supporting documents before any Customs query.

rules.title: Quantities and weights agree across invoice, packing list and transport document
rules.requirement: The permit declares total gross weight (tonnes for sea, kilograms for air) and item quantities in the prescribed units. This project assumes these figures are taken from the packing list and the bill of lading or air waybill, so those documents must agree.
rules.readiness_check: Line quantities on invoice and packing list are equal; packing-list gross weight is within 2% of the transport document.
rules.corrective_action: Reconcile with the supplier and the forwarder; obtain corrected documents.
rules.status_note: The guide defines the weight and quantity fields; it does not state a cross-document tolerance. The 2% tolerance is an assumption.

rules.title: Export permit before export
rules.requirement: Export permits are submitted before export (recommended before cargo lodgement with the port operator or air cargo handler); exceptions with post-departure deadlines exist for some bulk petroleum and chemicals and for steel bars. 'Submitting declarations only after export' is listed as a common offence.
rules.readiness_check: Export permit timestamp is earlier than the departure date.
rules.corrective_action: Apply for the export permit before lodging the cargo.

rules.title: Export clearance documents; low-value air exemption
rules.requirement: For clearance, the approved export permit and supporting documents such as commercial invoices and the bill of lading or air waybill are presented. A permit is not required for non-controlled, non-dutiable goods valued at S$1,000 or less exported by air; controlled goods and goods removed from licensed premises need a permit regardless of value.
rules.readiness_check: Export bundle has permit (unless exempt), invoice and BL/AWB.
rules.corrective_action: Request the missing document.

sources.where: containerised cargo; when no permit is needed

rules.title: Strategic goods: individual permit 5 working days before export
rules.requirement: For strategic goods under an Individual Permit of the Strategic Trade Scheme, the permit is submitted 5 working days before export.
rules.readiness_check: Manual: strategic goods are identified by the customer; not screened automatically.
rules.corrective_action: Plan the permit 5 working days ahead.
rules.status_note: The synthetic data contain no strategic goods.

rules.title: Singapore origin only when origin criteria are met
rules.requirement: Singapore may be declared as the country of origin only if the goods meet the FTA rules of origin (for preference in the partner country) or Singapore's non-preferential rules of origin; declaring goods as Singapore-origin when they do not qualify is on the 'do not' list, and a wrong origin is a common error.
rules.readiness_check: Exports declared as SG origin have an origin basis recorded (FTA rule or non-preferential CO).
rules.corrective_action: Correct the origin; apply for a certificate of origin if preference is wanted.

rules.title: Exporter is normally the invoicing party
rules.requirement: The exporter is usually the party issuing the commercial invoice to the overseas customer; a third party involved in exporting the goods may declare itself exporter when it acts on the invoicing party's behalf or consolidates for customers without a UEN. A UEN must not be used to export goods that do not belong to that entity unless it acts as exporter or consolidator.
rules.readiness_check: Exporter UEN on the permit equals the invoicing customer's UEN.
rules.corrective_action: Correct the exporter fields.

rules.title: Export documents within 14 days after departure
rules.requirement: 'Failing to submit export documents within 14 days after vessel or aircraft departure' is listed as a common offence.
rules.readiness_check: Manual reminder in the action log 14 days after departure.
rules.status_note: The wording is on the page, but the page does not say which documents or to whom, so the rule is not automated.

rules.title: Declaration type by value: Import Declaration above AUD 1,000
rules.requirement: An Import Declaration (N10) is required when a consignment has a combined value over AUD 1,000 and is cleared into home consumption; duties, taxes and charges, including an import processing charge, are paid before release. Air and sea cargo of AUD 1,000 or less uses a Self-Assessed Clearance declaration; goods that need a permit use an N10 or a long-format SAC. Tobacco and alcohol bear duty and taxes regardless of value.
rules.readiness_check: For SG-to-AU shipments the expected declaration type is derived from the AUD value and the permit flag.
rules.corrective_action: Tell the consignee's broker which declaration type applies.

rules.title: Documents for an Import Declaration; keep five years
rules.requirement: Lodging an Import Declaration in person needs the bill of lading or air waybill, the commercial invoices, evidence of identity, permits or approvals and other relevant documents; all relevant documents are kept for five years after the declaration.
rules.readiness_check: SG-to-AU export bundle includes invoice, BL/AWB and any AU permit.
rules.corrective_action: Send the missing document to the consignee's broker.

rules.title: Customs value: transaction value on an FOB basis
rules.requirement: The usual method (transaction value) is based on the price actually paid or payable, with adjustments, provided the buyer-seller relationship does not influence the price. Australia's customs value is an FOB valuation: it excludes international freight and insurance from the place of export.
rules.readiness_check: For SG-to-AU shipments the invoice value is converted to an FOB customs value: CIF/CIP/CFR/CPT/D-term invoices need the freight and insurance shown separately so they can be deducted.
rules.corrective_action: Ask the customer to show freight and insurance separately on the invoice.
rules.status_note: FOB basis verified against the ABS methods publication; the ABF valuation fact sheet (PDF) could not be read here.

rules.title: GST 10% of the value of the taxable importation
rules.requirement: GST on taxable importations is 10% of the value of the taxable importation: customs value + international transport and insurance (to the extent not already in the customs value) + customs duty + any wine equalisation tax.
rules.readiness_check: Estimated AU GST = 10% x (FOB customs value + T&I + duty) in AUD.

sources.where: 'How much GST do I have to pay?'

rules.status_note: Duty is set to 0 in the synthetic data (tariff rates are not modelled).
assumptions: Customs duty = 0 for all synthetic AU lines.

rules.title: ABN on the import entry
rules.requirement: An importer that has an ABN supplies it when formally entering goods; an ABN and GST registration are needed to claim input tax credits or use GST deferral. Importers not entitled to an ABN are identified with customs owner codes.
rules.readiness_check: Consignee ABN (or owner code) recorded for SG-to-AU shipments.
rules.corrective_action: Ask the consignee for its ABN.
rules.status_note: The synthetic data only record whether an ABN was provided, never an ABN number.

rules.title: Self-assessed tariff classification under the Customs Tariff Act 1995
rules.requirement: Imported goods are classified under the Customs Tariff Act 1995; importers self-assess the classification (the Working Tariff is the online version), penalties may apply for incorrect or misleading information, and advance rulings are available through the Tariff Advice system.
rules.readiness_check: First 6 digits of the AU tariff code are a valid HS 2022 subheading.
rules.corrective_action: Correct the classification; use Tariff Advice for doubtful products.
rules.status_note: The requirement is verified. Australia's national digits (8-digit tariff subheading plus statistical code) were not checked against an official page, so only the HS 6-digit prefix is validated.

rules.title: Biosecurity import conditions (BICON)
rules.requirement: Some goods are subject to biosecurity import conditions by law: some are not permitted, others need supporting documentation, treatment or a biosecurity import permit; BICON is used to find out which. Most permits are issued within 20 business days for standard (category 1) applications and within 40 for non-standard ones, after payment and a complete application.
rules.readiness_check: SG-to-AU lines in screened chapters (food, plants, animal products, wood, raw fibres) need a BICON check recorded in the handling note.
rules.corrective_action: Check BICON for the commodity and obtain the permit or treatment certificate it asks for before shipping.

sources.where: Importing into Australia; Biosecurity import permits

rules.status_note: Requirement verified; the chapter screening list (rules/au_biosecurity_screening.csv) is this project's heuristic. It cannot see packaging such as timber pallets, nor timber goods classified outside the screened chapters (for example wooden furniture in chapter 94).

rules.title: Prohibited and restricted goods need permission
rules.requirement: No general import licence is needed, but some goods need permits regardless of value. For prohibited or restricted goods the importer must get permission from the relevant government department or agency and provide proof of it to the ABF.
rules.readiness_check: Manual: AU restrictions are not screened automatically; the handling note asks the consignee to confirm.
rules.corrective_action: Obtain the permission before shipping.

rules.title: Claim FTA preference only with evidence of origin
rules.requirement: Preferential tariff details should not be entered unless there is appropriate evidence that the goods meet the rules of origin, for example when the certificate or declaration of origin is not available; the origin country is still entered and the general rate applies. The Singapore-Australia FTA uses ICS preference scheme code SFTA and AANZFTA uses AANZ.
rules.readiness_check: If the customer asks for AU preference, a certificate or declaration of origin is on file.
rules.corrective_action: Obtain the origin document; otherwise the consignee declares the general rate.
rules.status_note: On the ABF page the key sentence reads 'should not be input ... if appropriate evidence that the goods meet the rules of origin' and appears to omit a word; the next sentence (certificate or declaration of origin not available) supports the reading used here.

rules.title: Trade description labels for certain goods
rules.requirement: Certain imported goods must carry a trade description in English that includes the country where they were made or produced (and a true description where required); goods that need a label but are not labelled may be seized.
rules.readiness_check: Manual: labelling is confirmed with the customer for consumer goods.
rules.corrective_action: Relabel before shipping.
